body:
The diagram below shows how old mobile phones are recycled at a specialist recycling plant.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Recycling old mobile phones at a specialist plant
steps: Old phones are collected through shops, post and recycling bins
Phones are sorted by model and checked for reuse
Phones that still work are cleaned, tested and resold
Batteries are removed and sent for separate treatment
Screens and casings are separated by hand or by machine
Circuit boards are shredded into small fragments
Metals are separated using magnets and chemical baths
Fragments that fail a purity test are returned for shredding
Recovered gold, copper and other metals are sold to refiners

body:
The diagram below shows the stages in printing and distributing a daily newspaper.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Printing and distributing a daily newspaper
steps: Stories and photographs are filed to the newsroom system
Editors check the copy and design each page on screen
Finished pages are sent electronically to the printing plant
A printing plate is made for each page
Plates are fitted to rotary presses that print onto reels of paper
Printed sheets are folded, cut and stacked into bundles
Bundles are wrapped and loaded onto delivery vans
Vans take bundles to local depots, where newsagents collect them
Newsagents and delivery drivers sell or deliver copies to readers
Unsold copies are returned to the depot and recycled

The plans below show an office floor in 2015 and in 2024, after it was converted to an open-plan layout.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: Office floor layout before and after conversion to open-plan

features: Ten small private offices along the north wall
Reception desk next to the main entrance in the south-west corner
Two meeting rooms in the centre of the floor
Long corridor running east to west through the middle of the floor
Kitchen and staff room in the east, next to the lifts
Printing room in the north-east corner
Storage cupboard behind the reception desk
Terrace accessed through a door in the south-east corner
Private offices removed and replaced by open desks along the north wall
Reception desk unchanged next to the main entrance in the south-west corner
Two meeting rooms in the centre replaced by one large room with glass walls
Corridor removed to create one open workspace across the floor
Kitchen extended eastwards with a larger dining area
Phone booths for private calls added along the west wall
Printing room unchanged in the north-east corner
Terrace in the south-east corner now used for outdoor lunch tables

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: A former post office building, 2010 and today

features: Sorting hall occupying most of the ground floor
Public counter along the front wall, facing the high street
Parcel store at the back, next to the loading bay
Two small offices on the first floor above the counter
Staff car park behind the building
Loading bay on the east side for post vans
Clock tower on the roof above the main entrance
Cellar used to store old records in the north-west corner

after.label: Today
features: Sorting hall divided into open co-working desks across the ground floor
Public counter removed, and the front wall now has a café and reception desk
Parcel store at the back converted into a digital skills training room
Two first-floor offices joined into a glass-walled meeting room
Staff car park behind the building turned into a bicycle store
Loading bay on the east side kept for deliveries
Clock tower unchanged on the roof above the main entrance
Cellar converted into showers and lockers for cyclists in the north-west corner
